transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-15
Start time: 10:07 AM UTC
Duration: 55 minutes (approx)
Attendees: Alex Kim, Priya Desai, Daniel Park, Maria Lopez, Samir Patel, Elena Rossi

Summary:
Quick sync to run through Q2 roadmap items tied to the upcoming v1.3 product launch, confirm infra scaling and launch readiness, review the March 3 incident follow-ups, and finalize owners for the launch checklist. Some tangents about benchmarking, KV cache behaviour and config defaults.

Topics:
- Launch checklist / owners
- Dedicated vs hosted routing for canary
- Incident review (Mar 3 outage) and remediation status
- Perf benchmarks: QPS, tail latencies, batching behavior
- QA/regression and release gating

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex: Alright, uh, good morning everyone, thanks for joining. let's start, we have 55 minutes so I'll try to keep it tight. agenda — launch checklist, infra, incident follow-up, qa and then owners.
[00:28] Priya: Sounds good, Alex. quick note — I've got the infra notes from the SRE team, we ran a smaller scale bench this week, saw some tail-latency spikes when the prefix cache churned. might be kv cache warming related.
[00:46] Samir: yeah that's what I pulled — when we evict big prefix entries the kv cache sees a transient read amplification, which with our current batching policy shows up as 95th/99th tail. we're testing a different eviction window.
[01:14] Daniel: are these spikes persistent on request storms or only during model switchovers? my reading was during model variant rollouts.
[01:27] Samir: primarily during model switchovers and big sequence lengths, also when we drain a worker and its KV state isn't warmed on the new host.
[01:41] Maria: that's the Mar 3 incident tie-in right? that was a cascade from autoscaler frequently shifting pods under heavy burst, I think.
[01:54] Priya: yes, Mar 3 — autoscale policy + node drain + our current fallback routing caused backpressure. I have the timeline but the postmortem is still being finalized.
[02:10] Alex: okay, action: Samir to own the short postmortem TL;DR for stakeholders, Priya, please to adjust the autoscale thresholds.
[02:22] Samir: noted. I'll include the KV cache mitigation options — like softer eviction, pre-warm flows, and a temporary routing fallback to smaller model variants.
[02:36] Elena: from QA perspective, we need clear gating — release chess: nightly regression, integration smoke, and a canary ramp. I flagged a couple of prompts that are sensitive to quantization changes.
[02:54] Daniel: do we have a plan for model quantization profile for the v1.3 rollout or are we sticking to the current default?
[03:05] Alex: we have recommendations from research — default 8-bit quant for most models, but for latency-sensitive routes we'll keep FP16 on dedicated. we should map routes in the checklist.
[03:22] Maria: speaking of routes — for the canary, are we using hosted routing with policy-based fallback or dedicated-only?
[03:31] Priya: ops prefer dedicated for predictable p99 right now, but cost tradeoffs are significant. we proposed a hybrid: canary on dedicated (small pool), fallback to hosted with caching enabled.
[03:47] Samir: hosted fallback will add complexity for data residency + audit logs though. need to document for compliance.
[03:55] Alex: good call. add to checklist: verify audit log continuity when flapping between dedicated and hosted.
[04:07] Priya: on benchmarks — we ran a 10-minute 1k qps test across a dedicated 8-gpu pool, observed average token latency within target but 99th got up to 450ms under some burst scenarios.
[04:26] Daniel: 450ms 99th is concerning for the low-latency routes. what was batch size distribution?
[04:35] Priya: effective batch sizes were pretty variable — the mix of short and long sequences caused wide variance. continuous batching helps but we need smarter router hints to co-locate similar seq-len requests.
[04:50] Elena: QA can add sequence-length focused regression tests; we have a set of synthetic loads. I'll own adding those to the nightly suite.
[04:58] Alex: assign — Elena add to regression, Priya run targeted bench and send results.
[05:10] Maria: on release gating timeline — we need final owner map by next Wed (March 18) and a canary window March 24-26.
[05:22] Alex: is that still realistic given outstanding infra items?
[05:28] Priya: yes if autoscale thresholds and KV mitigations are in place plus the bench results show p99 improvements. otherwise we slide one week.
[05:38] Samir: also we need to ensure RBAC and SSO checks are green for private deployments — last-minute audit doc asks. I can confirm, but we rely on the security team for SOC2 evidence.
[05:53] Alex: note: security will need the list of endpoints and retention windows. Maria — can you coordinate with security?
[06:02] Maria: yes will do.
[06:07] [06:07] -- a short cross talk --
[06:25] Daniel: quick question on release versioning — are we doing canary flags with config-only changes or do we plan a model binary roll?
[06:36] Priya: mix: config-only for routing/quant flags initially, then small binary for model weights if needed. our router supports version pins so we can rollout by route.
[06:49] Alex: ok let's move to incident review specifics — Samir can you summarise the current remediation status for Mar 3?
[06:58] Samir: sure — root cause: aggressive autoscale draining combined with cold KV cache and a router fallback bug. mitigation in progress: 1) soften autoscale drain window, 2) pre-warm KV for drained nodes, 3) temporary stricter routing to avoid cross-region fallbacks. two are in test, pre-warm needs an infra change.
[07:25] Daniel: pre-warm sounds like it needs a service level change; do we have resource headroom to keep warm replicas?
[07:34] Priya: short term yes, but it's costy. we should measure cost delta and include in launch risk doc.
[07:44] Alex: add to risks: additional cost from warm replicas and potential longer rollout if pre-warm isn't ready.
[07:53] Maria: I'll put that into the launch risk slide and quantify.
[08:00] Elena: also we had a regression from a quantization tweak last sprint that slipped into canary test — I'm adding that as a gating check: no quant-related score drops beyond 2% for core prompts.
[08:15] Daniel: how are we measuring scoring; is it rouge-like or human evals? we have automated eval harness that approximates, but we need a human sample for launch.
[08:27] Alex: plan: automated regressions nightly, and a 50-sample human eval for final canary. we'll keep the eval harness config in the checklist.
[08:39] [08:39] -- time jump / later in meeting --
[20:02] Priya: results from earlier bench runs are in the doc I shared: two suggestions — 1) reduce batch timeout for low-latency routes and 2) pin small pool for critical routes to avoid noisy neighbors. both reduce cost efficiency slightly.
[20:20] Samir: prefer pinning for canary phase then explore dynamic sharing after launch.
[20:30] Maria: owners: Alex runs checklist, Priya runs infra bench, Samir writes postmortem TLDR, Elena QA tests, Daniel addresses router hints.
[20:42] Alex: ok capture that.
[20:47] Priya: another item — telemetry: we need per-route token-level cost breakdown in the console for the launch. currently retention defaults make it hard to slice per-route for 90 days. need a console telemetry change.
[20:58] Daniel: is that a console change or just an ETL tweak?
[21:04] Priya: small console UI plus backend retention change. estimate a few days of work.
[21:12] Alex: add as action item for product-infra pairing.
[21:19] [21:19] -- brief pause --
[31:05] Elena: QA notes — flagged two high-risk prompts that fail under long sequences with the new batching heuristic; I'll add the repro steps to the bug tracker.
[31:18] Daniel: I'll take a look and see if router hint heuristics can be improved to avoid mixing long+short in same batch.
[31:30] Maria: also we should prepare a stakeholder comms plan in case we need to delay. draft will be sent to execs and the sales lead.
[31:41] Alex: yes, Maria draft and we'll iterate.
[31:48] Samir: final point — KMS/HSM key rotation windows for private deployments. security asked for the rotation schedule in the launch docs. also need to confirm audit log continuity again if we fallback to hosted.
[32:03] Alex: Maria + Samir will coordinate and provide a blurb for the security pack.
[32:10] [32:10] -- wrap up segment --
[43:22] Alex: quick recap: Owners and due dates: Alex to circulate checklist (Mar 18), Priya run benches (Mar 20), Samir postmortem TLDR (Mar 19), Elena regression jobs (Mar 22), Daniel router hints (Mar 20), Maria update slides and security pack (Mar 17).
[43:45] Priya: noted. also will include the cost delta numbers after the pinning tests.
[44:00] Maria: I'll draft the stakeholder comms and share with Alex for review.
[44:12] Alex: any blockers we didn't cover?
[44:18] Daniel: nothing major, just need time on benches which Priya will set up.
[44:24] Samir: security sign-off timeline may be the gating factor for private customers, flagging that.
[44:32] Alex: ok. last thing — schedule follow-up next Tuesday same time to check progress.
[44:40] Elena: works for me.
[44:45] Alex: great, thanks all. end.
